question.text: Sundaram Industries Ltd (listed manufacturer) reports the following net profits (computed under Section 198 of Companies Act 2013): FY 2021-22 — INR 40 cr; FY 2022-23 — INR 50 cr; FY 2023-24 — INR 60 cr. For FY 2024-25 CSR budgeting under Section 135, what is the mandatory CSR spend?

answer.text: INR 1.00 crore — 2% of FY 2023-24 net profit only
INR 1.20 crore — 2% of FY 2024-25 projected net profit
INR 1.00 crore — 2% of the 3-year average net profit of INR 50 crore
INR 1.50 crore — 3% of the 3-year average net profit

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013, every eligible company must spend at least 2% of the average net profit of the three immediately preceding financial years on CSR. Average of 40 + 50 + 60 = 150 / 3 = INR 50 crore. 2% of INR 50 crore = INR 1 crore. Also, because the project spend is at least INR 1 crore, impact assessment by an independent agency is mandatory — a natural engagement pipeline for the SIA. The Trap: Using only the latest year ignores the 3-year averaging rule. The 3% rate is fabricated; the statutory rate is 2%. Forward-looking 'projected net profit' is never the basis. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser) tests CSR 2% when advising corporate clients. III-A/III-C (Compliance) tests LODR-side disclosure. XXIII frames it as how CSR inflows are reflected on the recipient NPO's books and in impact reports. Assessor's Pro-Tip: For a CSR project of INR 1 cr or more, the donor corporate must commission an independent impact assessment — this is the most common SIA engagement after SSE listings. Insist on the CSR agreement and the corporate's CSR-2 form to confirm the year of booking before you reference the inflow in your SAS-200/SAS-400 narrative.
